Cross-fitted GazeWeave analysis

Source: R/gaze_weave_cv.R
gaze_weave_cv.Rd

`gaze_weave_cv()` is the common entry point for the two GazeWeave engines. Use Transport for symmetric explanatory alignment and Replay for a directional encoding-to-recall model. There is no universal engine default; the supplied engine-specific specification selects the scientific model.

Usage

gaze_weave_cv(
  ref_tab,
  source_tab,
  match_on,
  contrast_on = NULL,
  refvar = "fixgroup",
  sourcevar = "fixgroup",
  spec = NULL,
  engine = NULL,
  split_on = match_on,
  n_folds = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  fit_source_filter = NULL,
  eval_source_filter = NULL,
  episode_on = NULL,
  priorvar = NULL,
  template_on = NULL
)

Arguments

ref_tab, source_tab

Reference and source tables.

match_on

One or more columns defining the true template match.

contrast_on

Optional columns restricting nonmatching candidates.

refvar, sourcevar

List columns containing fixation groups.

spec

A [gaze_transport_spec()] or [gaze_replay_spec()].

engine

Either `"transport"` or `"replay"`. When omitted, it is inferred from `spec`.

split_on

Columns defining the held-out unit. Defaults to `match_on`.

n_folds

Number of cross-fitting folds. `NULL` uses up to five; for Replay, which scores each held-out row against the candidates in its own fold, the default is lowered when needed so that every fold keeps a true candidate and a nonmatch in each contrast stratum. Calibration needs more: each training fold must hold at least `2 * calibration folds` items (4 by default) per contrast stratum, or that fold falls back to an uncalibrated score and a warning of class `gaze_calibration_fallback` is raised.

seed

Fold-assignment seed. `NULL` uses the engine-specific default. Folds depend on `seed` alone: the draw uses R's default generator and locale-independent ordering whatever `RNGkind()` and locale are in effect, and the caller's generator and random number stream are left unchanged.

fit_source_filter, eval_source_filter

Optional logical vectors or functions selecting fitting and evaluation source rows.

episode_on

Optional reference columns identifying separate study presentations for Transport. Their likelihoods receive equal prior weight.

priorvar

Optional Transport reference column containing one positive design-prior weight per candidate.

template_on

Optional reference columns identifying separate encoding templates of one candidate for Replay (the counterpart of `episode_on`); see [gaze_replay_cv()].

Value

An engine-specific fitted object. Use `broom::tidy()` for the sole primary endpoint, `gaze_info_bits`.

Details

Both engines return held-out candidate probabilities and `gaze_info_bits = log2(p_true / prior_true)`. Replay correspondence is a posterior probability. Transport correspondence is an optimized alignment and must not be interpreted as statistical uncertainty.

Result columns

Every GazeWeave fit (`gaze_transport_cv()`, `gaze_replay_cv()`, `gaze_baseline_cv()`) has `results` with one row per held-out source row (per source row and method for the baseline court) holding the source identifiers and these columns:

`.cv_fold`

Outer fold that held the row out.

`gaze_info_bits`

`log2(posterior_true / prior_true)`, the primary endpoint. `NA` for uncalibrated baseline methods.

`posterior_true`, `prior_true`

Held-out probability of the true candidate, and its declared prior.

`odds_bits`, `log_loss`, `brier_score`

Other proper scores of the same posterior.

`template_rank`, `top1_credit`

Rank of the true candidate (1 is best) and credit for ranking it first, split over ties.

`candidate_count`

Number of candidates scored.

`candidates`

Per-row table with at least `candidate_key`, `log_score`, `prior`, `posterior` and `is_true`.

Each engine adds its own diagnostics (for example Transport's solver counts or Replay's background level), documented on its own page. Every fit also has `spec`, `keys`, `folds` and `provenance`; `provenance$engine` names the engine, and Transport and Replay record their estimator `provenance$revision`.

Experimental

GazeWeave is experimental. Its interface, defaults and result columns may change in future releases; record the package version with any results.

Examples

# Example data: two participants study and later recall six images; each
# recall roughly repeats the study path of the same image.
set.seed(1)
make_path <- function(anchor, jitter) {
  fixation_group(
    x = anchor[1] + c(0, 2, 4, 3) + rnorm(4, sd = jitter),
    y = anchor[2] + c(0, 1, -1, 2) + rnorm(4, sd = jitter),
    onset = c(0, 250, 500, 750), duration = c(200, 220, 180, 240)
  )
}
study <- expand.grid(participant = c("p1", "p2"), image = 1:6,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
anchors <- lapply(study$image, function(i) c(3 * i, 2 * (i %% 3)))
study$fixgroup <- lapply(anchors, make_path, jitter = 0.2)
recall <- study[c("participant", "image")]
recall$fixgroup <- lapply(anchors, make_path, jitter = 0.6)
# \donttest{
# Which studied image does each recall come from? Candidates are the
# images the same participant studied.
fit <- gaze_weave_cv(study, recall, match_on = c("participant", "image"),
                     contrast_on = "participant",
                     # 2 coverage nodes keep the example fast; the
                     # default is 12.
                     spec = gaze_transport_spec(coverage_nodes = 2),
                     n_folds = 2)
fit
#> Cross-fitted GazeWeave Transport
#>   held-out rows: 12 
#>   primary endpoint: gaze_info_bits
#>   finite scores: 12 
#>   mean gaze_info_bits: 2.3153 
#>   episode normalization: fixed equal-prior likelihood mixture; one episode is the identity case
head(broom::tidy(fit))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   participant image gaze_info_bits
#>   <chr>       <int>          <dbl>
#> 1 p1              1           2.47
#> 2 p2              1           2.35
#> 3 p1              2           2.35
#> 4 p2              2           2.42
#> 5 p1              3           2.38
#> 6 p2              3           2.42
# }
